heroText: Orlando is a USA base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Walt Disney World Resort, add Universal Orlando Resort, and use International Drive to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Orlando International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

airports.text: Orlando International Airport is the main air gateway for Orlando; compare transfer time with your hotel base before locking the first night.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Orlando International Airport and central Orlando before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Orlando stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Orlando hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Orlando unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose City centre for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave extra time for Orlando International Airport, especially for early flights, late arrivals, traffic or unfamiliar transfer routes.

travelTips.title: Local movement
travelTips.text: Plan each day in clusters around Walt Disney World Resort and Universal Orlando Resort so transfers do not consume the best sightseeing hours.

travelTips.title: Day trips
travelTips.text: Keep one flexible slot for nearby routes from Orlando, checking weather, transport and opening hours before committing.

history.label: 19th century
history.text: Also, just south of the Orlando International Airport in the Boggy Creek area are 150 acres (0.61 km2) of property homesteaded in the late 19th century by the Ward family.
Fanning on November 9, 1838, during the construction of a series of fortified encampments across Florida during the Second Seminole War.
When the U.S. military abandoned the fort in 1839, the surrounding community was built up by settlers.
Fort Gatlin was briefly reoccupied by the military for a few weeks during October and November 1849, and subsequently a volunteer militia was left to defend the settlement.
In 1857, the post office was removed from Jernigan, and opened under the name of Orlando at a new location in present-day downtown Orlando.
For a short time in 1879, the town revoked its charter, and was subsequently reincorporated.
Orlando AAB and Pinecastle AAF were transferred to the United States Air Force in 1947 when it became a separate service and were redesignated as air force bases (AFB).

history.label: 1960s
history.text: In the 1960s, the base subsequently became home to the 306th Bombardment Wing of the Strategic Air Command, operating B-52 Stratofortress and KC-135 Stratotanker aircraft, in addition to detachment operations by EC-121 and U-2.

A major factor in Orlando's growth occurred in 1962, when the new Orlando Jetport, the precursor of the present-day Orlando International Airport, was built from a portion of the McCoy Air Force Base.
McCoy Air Force Base officially closed in 1975, and most of it is now part of the airport.

When McCoy AFB closed in 1976, its runways and territory to its south and east were transferred to the city to become Orlando International Airport, while a small portion to the northwest was transferred.
